## NEW FINDING

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.75
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35

FIND: `resolve_layer_conflicts()` at line 1068 joins kept directive blocks with `"\n".join(kept_texts)` instead of `"\n\n".join(kept_texts)`. The input blocks were split by `_split_packet_directives()`, which uses blank lines (`\n\n`) as block delimiters. After conflict resolution, blocks are rejoined with single newlines, destroying all intra-packet block boundaries. This means every packet that passes through `resolve_layer_conflicts` has its multi-block structure collapsed into a single block.

FOLLOW: Every call to `compose()` passes through `resolve_layer_conflicts`. This means ALL composed directive sets lose intra-packet block boundaries in their final text. Consequences:
1. The UNIVERSAL directive (HARD, containing the entire CDSFL core) has all its sections merged into one continuous text. Target models receive a wall of text instead of logically separated directive blocks.
2. If `_split_packet_directives` is called again on the output (e.g., during re-processing, debugging, or future pipeline stages), it sees 1 block per packet instead of N, changing pruning behavior and conflict detection.
3. The `_render_directive_text` function joins packets with `"\n\n---\n\n"` so inter-packet separation is preserved, but WITHIN each packet, all structure is lost.

ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. Demonstrated programmatically. Input: 3 blocks per packet. Output after `resolve_layer_conflicts`: 1 block per packet. The `"\n".join()` at line 1068 is the sole cause. The original `_split_packet_directives` requires `"\n\n"` (blank lines) to detect block boundaries, but the rejoin uses `"\n"` (no blank line). This is a HARD constraint violation: the composer docstring promises "deterministic" composition, but the block structure is not preserved through the conflict resolution round-trip.
